verdict.reasoning:
Rendered p. 927 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v927/spec_p927.png) and p. 926 at 200 dpi for the parent context, and read specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 37062-37120 directly.

The claim's two factual observations are accurate as far as they go. The PDF (printed page 897) does print items 1. through 7. at a deep third indent and then returns rules 6) and 7) to the outermost indent; the markdown at lines 37100-37118 does place all of them at column 0. But the finding is classified as 'misplaced-content' with 'structural' severity, and neither holds up.

NO CONTENT IS MISPLACED OR MISSING. Every item is present, in the correct order, with its label intact, bound to the correct neighbours. I compared all nine paragraphs word for word against the render: items 1.-7., the unnumbered continuation paragraph inside item 3 (which the markdown even indents 3 spaces, line 37106, to keep it bound to item 3), rule 6) ('shall not exceed 31'), rule 7) ('35 ... 34'), the 15.68.4 heading and its rules 1)-3). All match, including ISO's own typo 'the first three characters of local field int_curr_symbol' (PDF prints 'local', markdown reproduces 'local'). The sole difference is leading whitespace - i.e. exactly the 'formatting' class the verification rules say to reject.

THE HIERARCHY IS STILL RECOVERABLE, because the level markers themselves are what encode the level in ISO's scheme and they are transcribed faithfully: level 1 = 'N)', level 2 = 'x)', level 3 = 'N.'. The markdown preserves all three marker styles verbatim. Immediately before item 1., line 37093 reads 'b) The content of argument-1 shall be ... The following rules apply:' - so items 1.-7. are explicitly introduced as 'the following rules' of 5)b), by the sentence itself, not by indentation.

THE STATED CONSEQUENCE IS DEMONSTRABLY FALSE. The claim asserts that 'whether rules 6) and 7) apply to the LOCALE case only or to 15.68.3 as a whole is no longer recoverable from the markdown.' It is trivially recoverable: 6) and 7) continue the 1)-5) arabic-with-paren series of 15.68.3, and 5) is 'If the LOCALE keyword is specified, the following rules apply:'. A rule labelled 6) in the same series as 5) is necessarily a SIBLING of 5), never a child of it - the numbering alone settles it, with or without indentation. The subordinate rules of 5) are labelled a) and b), and the subordinate rules of b) are labelled 1. through 7.; none of those sequences could produce a '6)'.

IT IS ALSO NOT A PAGE-927 DEFECT. The same flattening is applied to the whole 15.68.3 rule block across the page boundary: on p. 926 the markdown puts 4)'s children a) through f) at column 0, 5) at column 0, and 5)'s children a) and b) at column 0, even though the PDF indents them at two distinct depths. So no content was displaced relative to its neighbours on page 927; a document-wide indentation convention was applied uniformly (repo-wide the transcription is inconsistent about this generally: 756 letter-level items are indented, 530 are at column 0).

The only residue is cosmetic: a CommonMark renderer will show the '1.'-'7.' list and the '6)'/'7)' list at the same visual depth, which looks odd. That is a rendering nit about leading spaces, not misplaced content, and it changes no normative meaning of 15.68.3 for an implementer.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. All nine rules on p. 927 are present, correctly ordered, correctly labelled and word-for-word faithful to the PDF (including ISO's own 'local field int_curr_symbol' typo). The difference is leading whitespace only: the markdown does not indent the level-2 and level-3 rule bodies. The nesting remains fully recoverable because the transcription preserves ISO's distinct level markers ('N)' / 'x)' / 'N.') and the introducing sentence 'b) ... The following rules apply:' at line 37093. The claim's stated consequence is wrong - rules 6) and 7) are unambiguously siblings of 5), and therefore apply to 15.68.3 as a whole, because they continue the same 1)-5) numbering series that 5) belongs to. The flattening is not local to page 927 either; the same convention is applied to 4)a)-f) and 5)a)-b) on page 926. If anything is worth logging, it is a low-severity, document-wide 'nested-list indentation not preserved' formatting note, not a page-927 structural misplacement.
